summary: Configured secure automatic synchronization of /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 to node2. Changes propagate immediately through a path watcher with a persistent five-minute timer fallback. Verified propagation in 5–6 seconds, including after sequential reboots of both nodes. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Initialized the previously absent authoritative file on node1 and synchronized it to node2.
Generated a dedicated Ed25519 synchronization key on node1.
Installed an atomic receiver on node2 with a source-IP-restricted, forced-command SSH authorization.
Enabled a systemd path watcher and persistent five-minute fallback timer on node1.
Verified matching file contents and SHA-256 hashes before and after changes.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities, recovered services, data, and synchronization.
Confirmed zero failed systemd units on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Synchronize node2 from node1 within 15 minutes
evidence.summary: Two source changes propagated with identical SHA-256 hashes in 5 and 6 seconds, including after both nodes restarted.
The restricted receiver, active/enabled watcher and five-minute timer, successful sync result, matching final data, and zero failed units were verified.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after restart; only already-installed OpenSSH and systemd facilities were used.
Captured healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered active/enabled synchronization units, successful post-boot sync, and matching destination data.
Captured healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered sshd/receiver/data, and a successful fresh synchronization after restart.
